findings.title: Pool becomes permanently unrefillable after any failed USE keyspace
findings.claim: The refiller stores current_keyspace before the USE result is known (root at connection_pool.rs:1287, also session.rs:2008) and never reverts it on failure; a connection whose USE fails is now discarded instead of admitted with a warning as before, and repeated failures can leave the pool permanently Broken(UseKeyspaceError).

findings.title: New error variant misapplied to non-connection-breaking keyspace failures
findings.claim: ConnectionError is documented as meaning the connection can no longer be used and should be dropped, but a nonexistent keyspace doesn't actually break the connection, yet it is now surfaced as the pool's broken reason through this variant.

findings.title: No timeout on the keyspace-setting future blocks refill scheduling
findings.claim: A hung USE future keeps is_filling() true and blocks all refill scheduling; this is a pre-existing TODO, but the PR makes this future the sole gate for admitting a connection, giving the issue more weight.

findings.title: Metrics rebalancing and decrement counts verified balanced, no double decrement
findings.claim: The metrics rebalancing in maybe_reshard, both excess-connection clears, and the keyspace-failure decrement are balanced, with no double decrement since remove_connection only decrements when it actually finds the Arc in conns or excess_connections.

findings.title: Keyspace check ordered before resharding avoids mutating sharder state for discarded…
findings.claim: Moving the keyspace check ahead of resharding correctly avoids mutating sharder state for a connection that is later discarded, as demonstrated by the second test.
